newsitem.title: UK: Conoco's North Sea Britannia gas pipeline installeD.
newsitem.headline: Conoco's North Sea Britannia gas pipeline installeD.

text.p: A new 27 inch pipeline has been installed to transport natural gas to mainland U.K. from the Britannia field, the largest undeveloped gas discovery in the U.K. North Sea, field operators Conoco (UK) Ltd said on Wednesday.

The 186 km pipeline, with a peak capacity of 740 million cubic feet per day, will come on stream in the second half of 1998 and will carry gas from Britannia to the Scottish Area Gas Evacuation System (SAGE) terminal at St. Fergus in Scotland.

Britannia has recoverable reserves of three trillion cubic feet of gas as well as an estimated 145 million barrels of recoverable condensate - a light crude oil - and peak production is expected to reach 50,000 barrels of condensate per day.
Field life is estimated at around 30 years.
Condensate will be exported via the Forties pipeline system.
The 44 km, 14 inch-diameter condensate pipeline from Britannia was installed at the end of April, Conoco said in a statement.
The Britannia field is to be operated by Britannia Operator ltd which is a joint venture of DuPont unit Conoco (U.K) Ltd and Chevron Corp's Chevron U.K. Ltd.
The two companies respectively have a 42.41 percent and a 30.20 stake in Britannia Operator.

The remaining share is split between Union Texas Britannia Ltd (with 9.42 percent,) Saga Petroleum (U.K.) Ltd. (9.01 percent, Phillips Petroleum Co U.K. Ltd (6.78 percent,) and Texaco North Sea (U.K.) Ltd (2.18 percent.)
